caption:
Sole trader? You can't pay yourself a wage.

You and the business are one taxpayer. The ATO treats any "wage" a sole trader pays themselves as a distribution of profit. It isn't a deduction, and there's no payslip, PAYG withholding or super guarantee on it.

What you're actually taxed on is profit: income minus expenses. Take out $500 a week or leave it all in the account, the tax is the same.

What is deductible: your own super contributions. Sole traders can usually claim them in their personal return, up to the $32,500 concessional cap (2026–27), where they're taxed at 15% in the fund. The catch: the money is locked away until you retire.

Paying yourself a real wage is something a company structure does, with its own costs and rules. Worth paying a registered adviser to set up properly if you get to that point.

Did you think your drawings were a business expense?
